name: Clustal
tip: People-search site. Tap FIND ME ON THIS SITE, or search your name on the site if that page will not open. If an entry there is you, tap View Full Record and copy that page's link. Open the Do Not Sell or opt-out link at the bottom of the page, paste the link, tap Remove My Info, add your email, then tap the link they email you. A second listing needs a different email address. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Men Stopping Violence (people directory)
tip: Despite the name, this site has a people directory showing addresses, phones and relatives. Tap FIND ME ON THIS SITE, or search your name on the site if that page will not open. If an entry there is you, tap View Full Profile and copy that page's link. Tap Do Not Sell My Info at the bottom, paste the link, add your email, then tap the link they email you. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: UNPAN (people directory)
tip: People directory showing address and phone history. Tap FIND ME ON THIS SITE, or search your name on the site if that page will not open. If an entry there is you, open it and copy that page's link. Tap Opt Out in the menu, paste the link, tap Submit Opt-Out Request, enter your email, then tap Confirm Request in the email they send. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: EveryJoe
tip: People-search site. Tap FIND ME ON THIS SITE, or search your name on the site if that page will not open, and open your record if one is there. At the bottom of that page tap Do Not Sell My Info, check the link in the box is your record, tap Submit, enter your email, then tap Delete My Info in the email they send. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: TruePeopleSearch.net (not the .com site)
tip: A separate site from TruePeopleSearch.com with its own list. Search your name, open your report and copy its link. Tap Remove My Info in the menu, open the form it links to, and paste the link there. Send one form for each report.

name: CheckPeople
tip: Enter your email, tick the box and tap Continue. The link they email you opens the removal tool, which asks for your legal name and date of birth to find your record.

name: UnMask
tip: Enter your email, tick the box and continue. The link they email you opens the removal tool: enter your name, city and state, pick your record and remove it. Expect a CAPTCHA or two.

name: IDCrawl
tip: Ties names to usernames and social profiles. Tap FIND ME ON THIS SITE, or search your name on the site if that page will not open. If something on that page is you, copy the page's link. Open the opt-out page, paste the link into IDCrawl Page URL, enter your email, tick I'm not a robot and submit, then tap the link they email you. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: InfoTracer
tip: Search your first name, last name and state. Tick Select Record on the line that is you (check the age and addresses), tap Remove Data, then Submit. The email box is optional.

name: SearchQuarry
tip: Same removal tool as InfoTracer, but its own list. Drag the slider to pass the human check, search your name and state, tick Select Record on your line, tap Remove Data, then Submit.

name: PrivateRecords.net
tip: Fill in only first name, last name, city and state, then tap Search. If you are listed, tap Remove on your card. The next form needs your email, name, address and phone. Leave the box about submitting on someone else's behalf unticked. Nothing is removed until you tap the link they email you, which can take 48 hours to arrive.

name: SpyFly
tip: Choose the request to remove your information, enter your details and tap Continue. Tap Remove on your record, then open their email straight away: the confirmation link expires after 60 minutes.

name: Social Catfish
tip: Pick your state, enter your name and email and tap Submit Now. The profile link, photo and other boxes are optional, so leave them empty.

name: PropertyRecs.com
tip: Property records tied to your name. Enter your full name and city, tap Search, then tap Remove My Info on each card that is you. No email is needed. Wait for the Success message.

name: PropertyRec.com (sister site)
tip: Sister site of PropertyRecs with its own list. Same steps: search your full name and city, then tap Remove My Info on each card that is you.

name: United States Phone Book
tip: Old phone-book listings. A different site from USPhonebook. Search your last name and state, and clear the first-name box so a listing under an initial still shows. If your listing is there, tap REMOVE next to it. If it says there is no match, tap NOT LISTED.

name: People Data Labs (identity data)
tip: Sells identity profiles to other data companies. Choose Delete all my data and fill in your details. Leave Social URL empty, tick the three boxes, pick your state and tap Confirm Request. Then tap the link in their email, and the link in their text if you gave a phone number.

name: Pipl (identity data)
tip: Identity search sold to businesses and investigators. Set Type to Deletion. In Message type: Delete my data and do not sell it. Answer the sum and submit. They may email you to confirm.

name: FullContact (identity data)
tip: Identity data sold to marketers. Tap Delete My Data, enter your mobile number, tap Send Me A Code and type in the code they text you. Fill in the form that follows and submit. If it says the security check could not load, turn off your ad blocker or Brave Shields for this site.

name: Truecaller (caller ID)
tip: Caller ID app that puts a name to your number. Enter your number with +1 in front, tick the box, do the CAPTCHA and tap Unlist. If it sends a code to your phone or WhatsApp, type it in. It is done when it says the number is unlisted.

name: CallApp (caller ID)
tip: Caller ID app. Enter your number with +1 in front and tap Unlist.

name: OptOutPrescreen (credit offer lists)
tip: The credit bureaus' official site. It takes your name off the lists Equifax, Experian, TransUnion and Innovis sell for pre-approved credit and insurance offers. Choose the electronic opt-out for five years. The Social Security number and birth date boxes are optional.

name: Google: Results about you
tip: Not a broker. Sign in to Google, add your name, address, phone and email, and it lists search results that show them so you can ask for removal. That hides them in Google only, but it is a good way to spot brokers this list misses.
